fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline material class does not reconstruct the equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals.
The molecular-dynamics intervention and strain rates near 10^8 s^-1 are incompatible with the compression experiments conducted at approximately 10^-4 s^-1.
Grain-boundary sliding is inapplicable to the bulk single-crystal specimens and misses the composition-dependent dislocation mechanisms.
The hypothesis omits cryogenic inertial dulling, MSAD-controlled solid-solution strengthening, and high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier pinning.
explanation: The response only recognizes the broad idea that temperature affects plasticity through dislocation processes. It fails to identify the relevant FCC medium-/high-entropy single crystals, their orientation and initial state, the experimental temperature and strain-rate ranges, or the CRSS-based measurements. Its grain-boundary-sliding mechanism conflicts with the single-crystal system, while the predicted increase in high-temperature ductility does not capture the observed cryogenic strengthening, low-temperature inertial dulling, or modest serrated high-temperature strengthening. The proposed MD test is generic and operates in a fundamentally different rate regime, so it cannot discriminate the target mechanisms.
